verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas's own plan listings name 'Project Archive and Restore' and 'Download Apps for Self-hosting', and its SuperSplat Editor and SplatTransform export and convert splat data between formats. Together these show some first-party ability to take projects and data out of the hosted Editor. However, these are one-line plan bullets with no documentation of what an archive contains, whether it covers all user data, or whether it uses open formats. Community concerns about code living on PlayCanvas servers are general worry, not a concrete counter-example. Missing for 10: documented full-account or project export, confirmation that exported scenes and assets use open, non-proprietary formats, and independent or hands-on corroboration of leaving and self-hosting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: The SuperSplat Editor cleans up, crops, colors, animates and exports splats in the browser.
it converts between formats, transforms, filters and merges splat data
